Evaluating the block's OWN displayed formula at the proton pin gives S(q_0) = (2q+1-q^2)(q^2-1)/(2q^2) = 0.18720719, not 0.18689. The printed 0.18689 is instead Q_beta^CODATA/E_0(q_0) = 0.78233356/4.1859814 = 0.186893 -- i.e. the CODATA value divided by the substrate E_0, not the substrate ratio. The two differ by 0.168 percent, which is EXACTLY the Q_A-versus-CODATA gap this same block quotes two sentences later. So the block silently mixes its closed form with the experimental value in the one place it prints a number. Proposed fix: print S(q_0) = 0.18721 and, if the CODATA-over-E_0 quantity is what the SDP target actually is, name it separately. (2) 'PROVED' IS THE SUPERSEDED WORD. The block says 'The proved c_2 = -1 cannot be recovered this way.' The 2026-08-16 correction in AGENTS.md rules that 'PROVED' is wrong for c_2 -- the Lean is a one-line ring re-reading of the N=2 factor, with no theorem deriving it -- and that 'structural' is the defensible word. The sibling prop:q-beta-q-eq-one-shadow-gate already uses the corrected wording ('Taylor-exact for the explicit-factor product ... so the series must be named'), so this block is simply out of date. Proposed fix: 'The structural c_2 = -1 cannot be recovered this way.' Not fixed inline: it is a one-word epistemic-tier change and the tier vocabulary is registry-governed. Minor: 'the SDP-constraint scalar (canonical at q_0, ...)' is a low-confidence sweep-damage candidate where 'numerical at q_0' is the natural reading.
